page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. A catchword at the right foot.

main_text.l: Quid dicis de tertio Gradu?
Quando quis moritur non reliquis neque descen-
dentibus, neque ascendentibus, tum Collaterales, à le-
ge ad successionem defuncti, ab intestato, secundum
gradus prærogativam vocantur. Authen: cessante. C.
de legitim. hæredib.
Quinam intelliguntur appellatione
Collateralium?
Non solùm fratres & sorores, & omnes alii san-
guine juncti extransverso, sive sint propioris, sive ul-
terioris gradus in linea paterna, ad quam Agnati: aut
materna, ad quam Cognati referuntur. §. 1. instit: de
gradib. cognat.
Quot differentiæ inter fratres & sorores
recensentur?
Tres. Alii enim Germani dicuntur, qui ex uno pa-
tre & una matre prognati sunt, & hi alias utrinque con-
juncti vocantur, Brüder von vollet[?] geburt. Alii Con-
sanguinei, qui unum eundemque quidem habuerunt
patrem, sed diversas matres: Alii vero uterini, qui-
bus una est mater, sed non unus idemque pater.
Sequentes Regulæ sunt de collateralium
naturalium & legitimorum simul
successione obser-
vandæ.
Prima Regula.
Fratres & sorores utrinque conjuncti, sive sint legi-
timi & naturales simul, sive legitimati per subsequens
matrimonium, exclusis fratribus aut sororibus ex
uno latere conjunctis, defuncto fratri aut sorori succ-

page.notes: Running head is letter-spaced in print; given as DE RUDIMENTIS. Black letter German phrase: "vollet" is uncertain. The catchword "de quas" is partly cut off at the edge and is read as the start of "quaesitis". A dark handwritten or stain mark sits below the text, centre, and is not transcribed. A reddish stain lies near "differentiæ" and "fratres". Printed spelling "Regulæ" is kept. The long s is written as plain s throughout. The printed "Authen:" and "instit:" colons are kept as printed.
